items.followUp: State the main components of blood and give the approximate percentage of each component.

rubric.why: These are the two major components of plasma and their proportions.
rubric.description: Gives the percentages of water and plasma proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct component with its percentage.

rubric.why: The remaining plasma consists of dissolved substances.
rubric.description: Identifies the remaining 3% as other dissolved substances, such as salts, nutrients, hormones and wastes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the 3% remainder and/or suitable examples.

rubric.why: The diagram should represent the composition accurately and label its sectors.
rubric.description: Draws and labels a pie chart with correctly sized sectors for water, proteins and other solutes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct sector angles and 1 mark for clear labels.

modelAnswer: Plasma is the liquid part of blood.
It consists of about 90% water, 7% proteins and 3% other dissolved substances.
Other substances include salts, nutrients, hormones and waste products.
Pie-chart construction: draw a circle and mark its centre; use a protractor to make a 324° sector labelled Water (90%).
From the end of that sector, mark a 25.2° sector labelled Proteins (7%); the remaining 10.8° sector is labelled Other solutes (3%).
Add the title “Percentage composition of blood plasma.”
Diagram (not to scale): Water 90% | Proteins 7% | Other solutes 3%.

items.followUp: Name the vegetative and reproductive parts of a pea plant.

rubric.why: Roots, stems and leaves perform vegetative functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for roots, stem and leaves.

rubric.why: Flowers and the structures they produce take part in reproduction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for flowers and/or fruits and seeds.

modelAnswer: Vegetative parts of mustard are the roots, stem and leaves.
Reproductive parts are the flowers, fruits (pods) and seeds.

items.followUp: Name two tissues found in the small intestine.

rubric.why: The stomach has an epithelial lining.
Muscular tissue in the stomach wall helps mix and move food.

modelAnswer: Two types of tissues in the stomach are epithelial tissue and smooth muscular tissue.

items.followUp: State one difference between a colonial organism and a multicellular organism.

rubric.why: Colonial cells are grouped but retain considerable independence.
rubric.description: Describes the organization of a colony and the relative independence of its cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description.

rubric.why: Multicellular organisms have specialized, interdependent cells organized into higher levels.
rubric.description: Describes specialization and interdependence in multicellular organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast.

modelAnswer: In a colonial organism, similar cells live together in a group, but each cell can generally perform its life functions independently.
In a multicellular organism, cells are specialized and interdependent, and may be organized into tissues and organs.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a controlled experiment in biology?

rubric.why: Experiments are used to check whether a proposed explanation is supported.
rubric.description: States that experiments test a hypothesis.

rubric.why: Controlled conditions and observations allow results to be assessed reliably.
rubric.description: Mentions controlled conditions, observation or collection of results/data.

modelAnswer: Experiments are performed to test a hypothesis.
They are carried out under controlled conditions so observations or results can be used to judge the hypothesis.

rubric.why: A biological problem concerns living things or biological phenomena.
rubric.description: Identifies the subject of a biological problem as living organisms or biological phenomena.

rubric.why: A biological problem is an issue or question requiring investigation or a solution.
rubric.description: States that it requires investigation or solution.

modelAnswer: A biological problem is a question about living organisms or a biological phenomenon that needs to be investigated and solved.

items.followUp: What is a hypothesis, and how can it be tested?

rubric.why: A theory is an explanation or organized set of ideas about a phenomenon.
rubric.description: Describes a theory as an explanation or set of scientific ideas.

rubric.why: A productive theory leads to testable predictions or further hypotheses.
rubric.description: Explains that a productive theory generates testable predictions or hypotheses.

modelAnswer: A theory is a scientific explanation of a phenomenon based on evidence.
A productive theory can generate new hypotheses or predictions that can be tested by further experiments.

rubric.why: Phagocytosis is the uptake of solid particles by a cell.
rubric.description: Defines phagocytosis as engulfing solid particles or materials.

rubric.why: Pinocytosis is the uptake of liquid droplets by a cell.
rubric.description: Defines pinocytosis as taking in liquids or liquid droplets.

modelAnswer: Phagocytosis is the process by which a cell engulfs solid particles or materials.
Pinocytosis is the process by which a cell takes in liquid droplets.
